title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: Must go.mod require the runtime pin when no generated code imports the runtime library?
description: ST-GEN-INV13 says a generated service's module file MUST require the runtime library at its archetype's pin, and ST-SUP-INV10 says every service of the archetype MUST import that version. No shipped generator imports the runtime library yet, and go mod tidy, which stego deps runs, removes a requirement that no package imports, so stego deps then refuses the module because a compiler requirement is gone. Built now: the assembler adds the pin to go.mod and go.sum when a generated Go file, or an import that a wiring puts in main.go, is a package of the runtime library, and only then; every other STEGO module, another major version of the runtime library and a replace directive are refused or are drift in each case. Options: (a) keep it, and read INV13 as: when generated code imports the runtime library; it becomes the same as the statement once every archetype emits a runtime import; (b) require the pin always, and emit a file that imports the runtime library in every service, which is a static file (ST-SUP-INV12). Recommendation: (a).

title: Must the record hold the archetype and its runtime pin?
description: ST-SUP-INV10 says only a new archetype version moves the runtime pin, and ST-SUP-INV10-T expects a pin that moves within one archetype version to be refused. To see that, a run needs the archetype version and the pin of the last run, but the documented fields of the record (ST-GEN-EN01) hold neither, and ST-GEN-UC01-R04 lets no field change without a new format version. ST-DIS-RM01 also reads a Runtime version from the record. Built now: no new field; drift reads go.mod alone and finds a version that is not tagged, another STEGO module or a replace, but not a move from one tagged version to another. Options: (a) add to ST-GEN-EN01 the field Archetype (name, version, runtime pin, and whether generated code imports the runtime library), write it at record format version 3, and let the fleet sweep read versions 2 and 3; then apply refuses a moved pin and drift checks go.mod against the exact pin; (b) keep the record as it is, and leave the moved-pin part of ST-SUP-INV10 to the review of a registry change. Recommendation: (a), since the fleet's Runtime version needs it too.

title: How does a database in service move from the GORM tables to the SQL tables?
description: ST-SUP-RC01-OC41 makes 001_initial the SQL text of the tables, with the key id as uuid, a version column and no deleted_at, so its body digest differs from the GORM 001_initial in each database in service, and its tables differ from the GORM tables; the ledger refuses such a database with ErrMigrationLedger. Built now (ST-SUP-RC01-G20): the SQL tables only on the runtime data path, which the compiler does not switch on yet, so no database in service meets them, and ST-SUP-RC01-OC30 and OC31 keep the GORM baseline until the store retires. Options: (a) the compiler switches the runtime data path on only for a service whose base ref has no record, and a service in service stays on the store until it moves to a new declaration version (ST-GEN-UC10), whose new baseline is the SQL tables and whose migration converts the GORM tables, so that ST-GEN-INV35 holds across the move; (b) a postgres-adapter migration converts the GORM tables of every database in service in place, with a known-digest table as ST-SUP-RC01-OC31 has for 001_initial; (c) no migration: the operator dumps the rows and restores them into a new database. Recommendation: (a).

title: Which opener makes the pool of the runtime data path, and what keeps its verified TLS?
description: ST-SUP-RC01-OC41 says the pool is opened through tenant.Open (ST-SUP-RP04-LC08), and the command and query runtimes refuse any other pool. The adapter's opener OpenDatabase holds the verified TLS policy of ST-SUP-RC01-OC01 to OC04 and the pool bounds of OC12, but tenant.Open takes a tenant.Config with a DSN and applies no TLS policy of its own. Built now: the runtime data path keeps OpenDatabase for the migration job and for the wiring of main.go, and opens no pool through tenant.Open, because no code on that path reads the pool before the command and query generators (ST-SUP-RC32, ST-SUP-RC33) are built. Options: (a) tenant.Config takes a pgx connection configuration that the adapter's opener builds with its TLS policy and pool bounds, and the generated main.go opens the pool through tenant.Open with it, which is a runtime change; (b) the adapter emits an opener that refuses a DSN without sslmode=verify-full, calls tenant.Open with it and sets the pool bounds on the pool it returns; (c) the TLS policy moves into the runtime tenant package for every service. Recommendation: (a), wired in the change that switches the runtime data path on.
